Made by ____ and Forwarded by C.D.I. Ross

With reference to the article entitled "The
Shanghai People's Japanese Goods Boycott Group" published
in the "Morning Leader" (導報) of November 21, 1938, Mr.
Yang Ping (楊平), a reporter of the paper representing
Mr. Sanders-Pates, who was interviewed at headquarters on
November 30, explained that the article in question was sent
to the paper for publication in the form of a circular with
a covering note bearing the chop of the "Executive Committee
of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang" (中國國民黨上海
特別市黨部).
Mr. Yang, however, was unable to give the address of this
organ as the circular was delivered by hand.

Mr. Yang was warned that from the police point
of view the publication of such an article was highly
objectionable for it was an instigation to murder. Mr. Yang
expressed his regret and promised to transmit the warning to
Mr. Sanders-Pates.

November 21, 1938. Afternoon Translation.
Morning Leader and other local newspapers:-

THE SHANGHAI PEOPLE'S JAPANESE GOODS BOYCOTT GROUP

The Shanghai People's Japanese Goods Boycott
Group has issued the following declaration

"Final victory is being assured by the war of
resistance of the past sixteen months. The Japanese are
plundering, committing extortion and imposing cruel
taxes in the occupied areas. Worthless military notes are
being put into circulation everywhere.
"We have organized a Shanghai People's
Japanese Goods Boycott Group to deal with the brutal
enemy. In the work done in the past, the liquidation
of traitorous merchants is the most important. Their
secret activities are even more dangerous than those of
traitors and puppet officers. In order to get rid of
enemy goods from the market, we have first to liquidate
the traitorous merchants.
"We hope all patriotic people will help us to
mobilize and all professional youths will join in our
work and help to organize small units and co-operate with
one another.
"We would like to say the following words to
the traitorous merchants:- 'Although Shanghai is now in
a peculiar situation, the people will never abandon their
country. We will never forgive you. It is still
not too late to repent. We hope you will report to your
own association the amount of Japanese goods in your own
store and register them for the sake of your life.'"

（批：Sp B- V. bad stuff instigating to murder）

上海民众抵制日货团

上海民众抵制日货团发表如下宣言

“过去十六个月的抗战确保了最终胜利。日军在占领区进行掠夺、勒索并强征苛捐杂税。毫无价值的军用票到处流通。
“我们组织了上海民众抵制日货团以对付残暴的敌人。在过去的工作中，清除汉奸商人是最重要的一环。他们的秘密活动甚至比汉奸和伪职官员更为危险。为了将敌货从市场上清除，我们必须首先清除汉奸商人。
“我们希望所有爱国人士帮助我们动员，所有职业青年加入我们的工作，帮助组织小组并相互合作。
“我们要对汉奸商人说以下几句话：‘虽然上海目前局势特殊，但人民绝不会抛弃国家。我们绝不会原谅你们。现在悔改还为时不晚。希望你们向自己的同业公会申报店内日货数量并进行登记，以保全性命。’”

（批：特别处 - 内容极劣，煽动谋杀）

October 13, 1938.
Afternoon Translation

Morning Leader and other local newspapers:-

JAPANESE SEARCH FOR GUERRILLAS IN POOTUNG

On the night of October 9, mobile units attacked and inflicted heavy losses on the Japanese troops at Nan Mo Der (南碼頭) in Pootung. During the past few days, the Japanese have been searching the surrounding country for mobile units and failing to find any, they killed innocent people.

On the morning of October 11 one Yao (姚), age about 24, in whose home was found a brass gong, was taken away. After cutting off his nose the Japanese beheaded him.

At about 11 p.m. the same day, an old fisherman at Pei Tsai Village (北蔡鎮) was stopped by a party of 20 soldiers and asked where the guerrillas were. Not understanding Japanese, the old man did not answer, whereupon he was stabbed to death.

Yesterday morning four youths playing mah-jongg in a tea shop in Yao Ka Zah (姚家宅) were accused of being guerrillas and decapitated.

Two hundred houses in Pei Tsai Village (北蔡) were burned to ashes as a result of a fire set by Japanese soldiers at 11 p.m. October 11. The Japanese believed that the mobile units who had attacked them on the night of October 9 had come from that village.

《导报》及其他本地报纸：—

日军在浦东搜捕游击队

10月9日晚，机动部队在浦东南码头袭击日军，造成日军重大损失。在过去几天里，日军一直在周边乡村搜捕机动部队，因未能找到任何目标，便杀害无辜百姓。

10月11日上午，一名姓姚（Yao）的男子，年龄约24岁，因其家中发现一面铜锣而被带走。日军割掉他的鼻子后将其斩首。

同日晚上11点左右，北蔡镇的一名老渔夫被一队20名士兵拦住，询问游击队在哪里。老人不懂日语，没有回答，随即被刺死。

昨天上午，四名青年在姚家宅的一家茶馆里打麻将，被指控为游击队员并被斩首。

10月11日晚上11点，日军纵火，导致北蔡村两百间房屋化为灰烬。日军认为10月9日晚袭击他们的机动部队来自该村。

October 13, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

News Digest published the following article on Oct.12:

CONDITIONS IN WUSIH

Wusih is known as "Siao Shanghai". It was occupied by the Japanese in the latter half of November last year. During the first two weeks of its occupation, all persons with cropped hair like monks or attired in overalls were liable to arrest and execution on suspicion of being members of the Chinese army or mobile units. In all more than 1,000 such persons were killed.

The Lien Sin Cotton Cloth Factory in Wusih has been converted into a garrison post by the Japanese. Many people have been killed in this factory.

It happened that at first a farmer carrying a basket of vegetables was ordered to stop by an XX sentry and told to leave the vegetables and in return he was given a roll of cotton cloth. Gradually, the number of men began to increase and each was given a roll of cotton cloth in exchange for their wares. However, several days later, the men were separated from the women at the point of the bayonet. Adults and children were ordered to leave the place empty-handed, while the youths, both male and female, were taken into the factory and detained separately in two rooms. Needless to say, the women met a terrible fate. They were undoubtedly used to satisfy the lust of the soldiers, while all the young men were bound with wire and were later killed with machine guns on a piece of vacant ground by the side of the factory.

One day, the inhabitants of Wusih were told by the "Imperial Army" to call at the Foh Sing Flour Mill to receive free supplies of flour. Large numbers of persons called and were each given a packet of flour. On the following day, the callers were ordered to stand by the side of a huge pile of bags of flour. Members of the "Imperial Army" then mounted the pile and told the callers to seize what they threw down. The soldiers, however, overturned the mound of bags at one time and many persons were crushed to death.

《新闻文摘》（News Digest）于10月12日刊登了以下文章：

无锡之状况

无锡素有“小上海”之称。该市于去年11月下旬被日军占领。在占领后的头两周内，所有剃着和尚头或身穿工装的人，均因涉嫌为中国军队或流动部队成员而面临被捕和处决的危险。此类遇害者总计超过1,000人。

无锡的联申棉布厂（Lien Sin Cotton Cloth Factory）已被日军改为驻军据点。许多人在该工厂内遇害。

起初，一名提着菜篮的农民被某哨兵喝令停下，并被要求留下蔬菜，作为交换，他得到了一卷棉布。渐渐地，人数开始增加，每个人都以自己的货物换取一卷棉布。然而，几天后，男性和女性在刺刀的逼迫下被分开。成人和儿童被命令空手离开此地，而青年男女则被带入工厂，分别关押在两个房间里。毋庸赘言，妇女遭遇了可怕的命运。她们无疑被用来满足士兵的淫欲，而所有年轻男子则被铁丝捆绑，随后在工厂旁的一块空地上被机枪射杀。

有一天，无锡居民接到“皇军”的通知，前往福新面粉厂（Foh Sing Flour Mill）领取免费面粉供应。大量人员前往，每人获赠一包面粉。次日，这些前来领取的人被命令站在一堆巨大的面粉袋旁。“皇军”成员随后登上这堆面粉袋，告诉领取者去抢夺他们扔下来的东西。然而，士兵们一次性推倒了这堆面粉袋，许多人被压死。

July 22, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Morning Leader publishes the following manifesto dated
July 7, purported to emanate from the Preparatory Committee
of the Japanese, Korean and Formosan Anti-Fascist League :-

A MANIFESTO

Japan is the most ferocious and cruel
Fascist nation in the world. She has always had the
ambition to conquer the Far East and become the dominant
figure in Asia. With a view to bringing about the
realization of her plans, she is now engaged in a wholesale
aggression of China.

For the sake of international peace and
democracy, mankind should oppose the invasion of China
by the Fascist bandits of Japan and render every support
to China in her present war of resistance. The Japanese
Fascists have always had the intention of conquering
Annam, India, Siam, the Philippine Islands and other weak
nations in the Far East and in order to drive away the
influence of the Foreign Powers from the Far East; they
are not afraid to bring about a second world war.

All people, be they Japanese labouring
masses, or Koreans or Formosans, who are at present under
the oppression of the Japanese Fascists, should realize
the serious crisis. For the sake of our own existence
and emancipation as well as for the salvation of the Chinese
people, we must at once start a unified struggle against
the Japanese Fascist militarists. This is the only way
through which peace in the Orient can be assured.

We must first establish a united front
against the Japanese Fascist warlords pending the general
mobilization of all anti-Japanese-Fascist elements against
the Japanese militarists.

《晨导报》（Morning Leader）刊登了以下宣言，日期为7月7日，据称出自日本、朝鲜及台湾反法西斯联盟筹备委员会：

宣 言

日本是世界上最凶残的法西斯国家。她一直怀有征服远东并成为亚洲主宰的野心。为了实现其计划，她目前正对中国进行大规模侵略。

为了国际和平与民主，人类应当反对日本法西斯匪徒对中国的入侵，并全力支持中国目前的抗战。日本法西斯分子一直企图征服安南、印度、暹罗、菲律宾群岛及其他远东弱国，并为了驱逐列强在远东的影响，他们不惜引发第二次世界大战。

所有民众，无论是目前受日本法西斯压迫的日本劳苦大众，还是朝鲜人或台湾人，都应认识到危机的严重性。为了我们自身的生存与解放，以及为了拯救中国人民，我们必须立即开始统一斗争，反对日本法西斯军国主义者。这是确保东方和平的唯一途径。

在所有反日法西斯力量对日本军国主义者进行总动员之前，我们必须首先建立反对日本法西斯军阀的统一战线。

July 6, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Morning Leader publishes the following article written by one
Liu Lieh ( 劉易 ) :-

A CHAUFFEUR'S NARRATIVE

Tsing Wen ( 俊文 ), a chauffeur in the employ
of Japanese, came to see me to-day.
"I am sorry I could not come to Yangtsepoo
to see you", I said.
Before I could continue, Tsing Wen started
off on the following narrative :- "You would be enraged
if you had come. Once, while my car was waiting outside
the Shanghai Cotton Mill, I saw an Imperial soldier running
after a female worker, who was leaving the mill, with his
bayonet pointed at her. The soldier was only playing a
joke, but the female worker was so frightened that she
fell down. Raping, killing and other acts of ill-
treatment are common occurrences. It could not have
been worse in a world of beasts. The Japanese employees
of the mill whom I drive are known to me for more than
10 years. They have now changed their attitude. The
younger ones are the worst. They act so haughtily that
you would think that China has already been conquered.
"The Japanese mills are doing good business.
Sometimes, I am detailed to drive trucks. Besides the
--- Underwear Company, which has always been dealing in
Japanese goods, some well known native goods companies
are also buying Japanese goods. The best thing for the
Chinese people to do is not to buy new cloth for the time
being.
"On the night of June 1, a Japanese came to
tell me that Chinese aeroplanes were coming to drop bombs.
I secretly prayed that they would come quickly to kill
the enemy.
"I believe the Chinese troops will defeat
the enemy sooner or later. I would then drive my car
to welcome them or I could destroy the mechanism so as to
hamper the enemy."
I believe Tsing Wen is an ambitious chauffeur,
despite the fact that he is working for Japanese.

《晨导报》刊登了由刘易（Liu Lieh）撰写的以下文章：

一名司机的叙述

受雇于日本人的司机俊文（Tsing Wen）今天来看我。
“很抱歉我没去杨树浦看你，”我说。
没等我继续说下去，俊文便开始讲述如下内容：“你要是去了会非常愤怒。有一次，我的车在上海棉纺厂外等候时，我看到一名帝国士兵端着刺刀追赶一名离开工厂的女工。那士兵只是在开玩笑，但女工吓得摔倒在地。强奸、杀戮和其他虐待行为屡见不鲜。情况甚至比兽类世界还要糟糕。我开车接送的那些日籍工厂职员，我认识他们已超过10年。他们现在的态度变了。年轻的一辈最糟糕。他们表现得如此傲慢，让人以为中国已经被征服了。
“日本工厂生意兴隆。有时，我被派去驾驶卡车。除了那家一直经营日货的---内衣公司外，一些知名的国货公司也在购买日货。中国人目前最好的做法就是暂时不买新布料。
“6月1日晚，一名日本人告诉我，中国飞机要来投弹了。我暗中祈祷它们快点来杀死敌人。
“我相信中国军队迟早会击败敌人。届时我会开车去迎接他们，或者我可以破坏车辆机械装置以阻碍敌人。”
我认为俊文是一名有抱负的司机，尽管他为日本人工作。

Subject Morning Leader - editor warned regarding anti-Japanese article.

Made by D.S.I. Mackie Forwarded by C. [Signature]

With reference to the remarks of D.C. Special
Branch on attached article in the Morning Leader issue of
June 14th and in accordance with the instructions of A.A.
to D.C. Special Branch in connection with the attached
articles from the same source in the Morning Leader issues
of June 14th and 15th, Mr. Sanders Bates, editor of the
paper, was interviewed by D.S.I. Mackie and C.A. Loh
Sih-kya on 17.6.38.

Mr. Bates stated that the Hankow correspondence
consisted of the exchange of clippings between the editor
of the Wuhan Daily News (武漢日報) and himself.
He then produced clippings of articles from the Hankow
paper from which the attached articles were reproduced.
The material had been sent by mail to this port. The
clippings were examined by C.A. Loh Sin Kya who stated
that they appeared to be genuine.

Nevertheless Mr. Bates was informed that as he
was not in a position to confirm or refute the material
in the articles, he should not publish them especially
as they contained rabid anti-Japanese sentiments. It
was further explained to Mr. Bates that the fact that the
articles were published by a Hankow newspaper would not
absolve him of the responsibility for allowing his paper
to be the medium of what was nothing less than anti-Japanese
propaganda.

Mr. Bates stated that he would not be using the
Hankow correspondence in future, as he required the space
for local news.

日期：1938年6月18日
主题：《晨导报》——因反日文章警告编辑。

由特别支部警探 Mackie 制作。由 C. [签名] 转呈。

鉴于特别支部副督察长对6月14日《晨导报》上附件文章的评语，并根据行政助理（A.A.）就6月14日和15日《晨导报》上来自同一来源的附件文章向特别支部副督察长发出的指示，特别支部警探 Mackie 和华探长 Loh Sih-kya 于1938年6月17日约谈了该报编辑 Sanders Bates 先生。

Bates 先生表示，汉口通讯内容由《武汉日报》编辑与他本人之间交换剪报组成。随后他出示了汉口报纸上的文章剪报，附件中的文章即转载自这些剪报。这些材料是通过邮寄方式寄至本埠的。华探长 Loh Sin Kya 检查了这些剪报，并表示它们看起来是真实的。

尽管如此，Bates 先生被告知，由于他无法证实或反驳文章中的材料，他不应当发表这些文章，尤其是因为它们包含极端的反日情绪。此外还向 Bates 先生解释，文章由汉口报纸发表这一事实，并不能免除他允许其报纸成为不折不扣的反日宣传媒介的责任。

Bates 先生表示，他今后将不再使用汉口通讯内容，因为他需要版面刊登本地新闻。

Morning Leader (Hankow correspondence) :- 14 JUNE 1938 (P+)
ALLEGATION MADE THAT JAPANESE KILL PRISONERS
OF WAR

On June 2, I visited an exhibition of war
trophies (which is not yet open to the public) at Hankow.
In addition to the various kinds of war implements, there

were hundreds of diaries and letters all of which were
filled with anti-war sentiments and which also furnished
strong evidence of the killing of prisoners and civilians,
the raping of women and the sustaining of heavy losses
by the Japanese troops.
The following are a few examples:-
(1) Diary of a soldier of the 10th Japanese
Division contained the following record of an address
delivered by his Commander:- "Any officer or soldier who
is unpatriotic or who shrinks at fighting or who commits
an uncivilized act (raping or looting) will be executed."
This indicates the low morale among the Japanese troops.
(2) In another diary, the losses of the 5th
Division at Yikow were recorded: "Our brigade headquarters
were surrounded on March 27 and we could not send help.
We suffered heavy losses."
(3) Many licentious love letters were recorded
in the diary of a soldier of the 5th Division.
(4) Diary of a soldier of the medical corps,
dated January 7: "All members of our corps who have
completed their terms of service desire to return. I
wish that my term will be up soon."
(5) Diary of a soldier of the 5th Division:
"October 6. Killed 20 slightly wounded enemy soldiers
at Luchiachwang ( 呂家莊 ); they were prisoners."
(6) Diary of a soldier of the 5th Division:
"Visited the war relics at Taiyuan on November 20. The
sight was terrible. The Idahara Detachment alone lost
750 men killed."
(7) Diary of a soldier of the 5th Division:
"Burned down all the houses and killed all the residents,
consisting of about 250 persons, including women, children
and old people, at a village near Ta Ling ( 大嶺 ) on
January 31......It was really an interesting day."
(8) Diary of an officer of the 14th Division:
"Lost 700 men killed and wounded at the battle of Yuan
Shih ( 元氏 ) on December 12. Killed 300 Chinese prisoners
on the same day."

指控日军杀害战俘

6月2日，我参观了汉口的一处战利品展览（该展览尚未对公众开放）。除了各种战争器械外，还有数百本日记和信件，其中充满了反战情绪，并提供了日军杀害战俘和平民、强奸妇女以及遭受重大伤亡的有力证据。
以下是几个例子：
(1) 日本第10师团一名士兵的日记中记录了其指挥官的一次讲话：“任何不爱国、畏战或实施不文明行为（强奸或抢劫）的军官或士兵将被处决。”这表明日军士气低落。
(2) 在另一本日记中，记录了第5师团在 Yikow（音译）的损失：“3月27日，我旅指挥部被包围，我们无法派出援军。我们遭受了重大损失。”
(3) 第5师团一名士兵的日记中记录了许多淫秽的情书。
(4) 医疗部队一名士兵的日记，日期为1月7日：“我部所有服役期满的成员都希望回国。我希望我的服役期尽快结束。”
(5) 第5师团一名士兵的日记：“10月6日。在吕家莊（Luchiachwang）杀害了20名受轻伤的敌军士兵；他们是战俘。”
(6) 第5师团一名士兵的日记：“11月20日参观太原的战地遗迹。景象可怕。仅饭原支队（Idahara Detachment，音译）就有750人阵亡。”
(7) 第5师团一名士兵的日记：“1月31日____，在大嶺（Ta Ling）附近的一个村庄，烧毁了所有房屋并杀害了所有居民，包括妇女、儿童和老人在内约250人。这真是有趣的一天。”
(8) 第14师团一名军官的日记：“12月12日，在元氏（Yuan Shih）战斗中，伤亡700人。同日杀害300名中国战俘。”

June 14, 1938. Morning Translation.

Morning Leader (Hankow correspondence) :-

MANIFESTO ISSUED BY FORMOSAN REVOLUTIONARY PARTY

The following manifesto has been issued by
the headquarters of the Formosan Revolutionary Party :-
"The Japanese barbarians received their
civilization from China. Instead of repaying China,
Japan is now attacking her. Such kind of behaviour is
below that of the beasts.
"China is generous and peace-loving; so she
has always tried to move the troublesome Japanese by kind-
ness; but Japan is incorrigible.
"Owing to misgovernment by the Tsing
Dynasty, our 5,000,000 fellow-countrymen in Formosa were
ceded to the dwarf bandits. At that time, many persons
sacrificed their lives. It is the blood of these martyrs
that is inspiring the Formosan Revolutionary Party to-day.
"The Formosan Revolutionary Party is formed
by patriotic people of Formosa to save the descendants
of China from suffering at the hands of an alien people.
For several years we have suffered oppression, detention,
torture and massacre by the dwarf imperialists but we
have not lost our courage.
"History relates how Chu (楚), a small
county, was able to ruin Chin (秦). Why cannot the
5,000,000 people in Formosa avenge themselves? Why must
we submit to the Japanese bandits? Let everyone of us
be determined to die and overthrow the dwarf bandits.
"The mission of our Party is to strive for
revenge, independence and the restoration of Formosa to
China, and to support General Chiang Kai-shek in China's
war of resistance. We are fighting the dwarf bandits
for justice and for the small nations of the world.
Brethren of Formosa! If you do not want your descendants
to be slaves of the dwarf bandits, you should support
your motherland, 'sleep on the enemy's skin and eat the
enemy's flesh.'

June 3, 1938."

（左侧印章内容：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / 15 JUNE 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

《晨报》（汉口通讯）：-

台湾革命党发布宣言

台湾革命党总部发布了以下宣言：
“日本野蛮人从中华文明中接受了教化。日本非但不报答中国，反而现在攻击她。这种行为连禽兽都不如。
“中国慷慨且热爱和平；因此她一直试图以善意感化麻烦的日本；但日本不可救药。
“由于清朝政府治理不善，我们在台湾的500万同胞被割让给矮匪。当时，许多人牺牲了生命。正是这些烈士的鲜血激励着今天的台湾革命党。
“台湾革命党由台湾爱国人士组成，旨在拯救中华子孙免受异族统治之苦。多年来，我们遭受矮人帝国主义的压迫、拘留、酷刑和屠杀，但我们并未丧失勇气。
“史书记载，楚（Chu）这样一个小县如何能够灭掉秦（Chin）。为什么台湾的500万人民不能报仇雪恨？我们为什么要向日本强盗屈服？让我们每个人都下定决心，誓死推翻矮匪。
“我党的使命是为复仇、独立以及将台湾归还中国而奋斗，并支持蒋介石将军在中国的抗战。我们为正义和世界上的小国而与矮匪作战。台湾的兄弟们！如果你们不想让你们的后代成为矮匪的奴隶，你们就应该支持你们的祖国，‘卧薪尝胆’（原文为：睡在敌人的皮上，吃敌人的肉）。”

1938年6月3日。”

Standard (Comment) :-

THE TOMBS FESTIVAL DAY

The tombs festival is approaching and
people are making paper ingots. This will be the
second festival since the outbreak of hostilities.
Last year, we were not able to visit our ancestors'
tombs in Nantao or Chapei; this year we still cannot
go there. We do not know whether these tombs are intact.
The armed invasion of China by the enemy
has reduced Kiangnan to ashes. The dead cannot be
comforted, while those living have no means of making
a living. Can we ever forget this?
Those who make joss paper ingots should
stop doing so. We should save the money for the
purchase of munitions. This may console the souls of
our ancestors.

《标准报》（评论）：-

清明节

清明节将至，人们正在制作纸元宝。这是战事爆发以来的第二个清明节。去年，我们无法去南市或闸北祭扫祖先的坟墓；今年我们仍然无法前往。我们不知道这些坟墓是否完好无损。
敌人的武装入侵使江南化为灰烬。死者不得安宁，而生者无以为生。我们怎能忘记这一点？
那些制作冥币纸元宝的人应该停止这样做。我们应该省下这笔钱购买军火。这或许能慰藉我们祖先的在天之灵。

With reference to the attached translations of two
reports entitled "Mutiny among Japanese Soldiers in Kiangyin"

January 24 and 25 respectively, Mr. H.M. Cumine, Chief Editor

when he was warned that the publication of articles of this
nature was highly undesirable.

exercise greater care in future. He stated that in consequence
of failing to observe his repeated instructions regarding
the publication of articles of a political nature, he had
dismissed the following employees on February 1:-

8) Ma Chih-shan (馬直山), reporter.

Mr. C.C. Hsu (徐鑄成) would be the chief Chinese editor of
the "Standard".

Standard (Foochow telegram) :-

MASSACRE OF 200 CHINESE ON A BRITISH SHIP

The other day about 270 Chinese from the South
Sea Islands left Rangoon for China on the s.s. "Haimen" (海门)
of the "Teh-Ji-Li-S" Company (德忌利士公司), a British concern.
On January 14 when the vessel arrived outside Swatow harbour,
she was stopped by two Japanese submarines. Immediately
afterwards a large number of Japanese marines boarded the
vessel and bound all the passengers. With the exception of
60 Chinese, who were natives of Fokien, the remaining 200
passengers, most of whom are natives of Kwangtung, were
mercilessly massacred on board. The Captain of the ship
was also wounded, while the cargo was carried away.
This is another instance of Japanese brutality
and cruelty.

《标准报》（福州电报）：-

英轮上200名中国人被屠杀

日前，约270名来自南洋的华人乘坐英国德忌利士公司（Teh-Ji-Li-S Company）所属的“海门”号（s.s. "Haimen"）轮船，从仰光前往中国。1月14日，当该船抵达汕头港外时，被两艘日本潜艇拦截。随即，大量日本海军陆战队员登船，将所有乘客捆绑。除60名福建籍华人外，其余200名乘客（大多为广东籍）在船上被无情屠杀。船长也受伤，货物被掠走。
这是日本暴行和残酷的另一例证。

MUTINY AMONG JAPANESE SOLDIERS IN KIANGYIN

The other day a mutiny broke out among the
entire body of 500 Japanese soldiers stationed at Kiangyin Sp Bn
(江陰), in the course of which the Japanese Commander was
killed. The mutineers then began to plunder, rape and Comr ?
massacre and set fire to houses in the city. The
insurrection was quelled by Japanese forces sent from
Wusih who succeeded in rounding up the mutineers and
placing them on a boat for Shanghai.
It is learned that the mutiny was due to

Standard of January 29 published the following drama :-

"THE COMMON ENEMY"

Time : January 28 of the 28th Year of the Chinese Republic.
Place : In an occupied village.
Dramatis Personae : A Chinese boy of 11 years of age
                   A Chinese girl of 9 years of age
                   An XX boy of 10 years of age
                   A Korean boy of 10 years of age

Scenery: A meadow surrounded by hills covered with trees.

The curtain rises on the Chinese boy holding a
Chinese flag followed by his younger sister.

The Boy : Sister, to-day is the anniversary of the January 28
          Incident. On this date the aggressors massacred our
          fellow countrymen in Shanghai. At that time we did
          not fight them because we were not prepared. To-day
          we are engaged in a life and death struggle with
          them. Although our homes have been destroyed,
          there is a bright future for our country. Come,
          let us hoist this national flag on a tree and
          salute it.

The Girl : How are we to hoist the flag on the tree? Oh, I
           have an idea. You stoop near the tree and I will
           hoist it by standing on your shoulders.

(The flag is hoisted and it flies under the shining sun)

The Boy : Sister, let us salute the flag.

          The boy and the girl here sing :-

          The national flag is flying in the air
          Brother and sister, hand in hand,
          Make three bows before it.
          First bow, may the national revolution succeed,
          Second bow, may the Imperialists lose their
                    arrogance,
          Third bow, help the weak and suppress the strong.

(A Korean boy and an XX boy are seen approaching from
 behind the trees)

Chinese Girl : Brother, here come two dwarves!
Her brother : Let us assault the dwarves!

1月29日的《标准报》刊登了以下剧本：-

“共同的敌人”

时间：中华民国二十八年一月二十八日。
地点：在一个被占领的村庄。
人物：一名11岁的中国男孩
      一名9岁的中国女孩
      一名10岁的XX男孩
      一名10岁的朝鲜男孩

布景：四周环绕着树木覆盖的山丘的草地。

幕启时，中国男孩手持中国国旗，身后跟着他的妹妹。

男孩：妹妹，今天是“一·二八”事变纪念日。在这一天，侵略者在上海屠杀了我们的同胞。那时我们没有与他们战斗，因为我们没有准备。今天，我们正在与他们进行生死搏斗。虽然我们的家园被毁，但我们的国家有一个光明的未来。来，让我们把这面国旗挂在树上，并向它致敬。

女孩：我们怎么把旗子挂到树上呢？哦，我有个主意。你在树旁弯下腰，我站在你的肩膀上把它挂起来。

（旗帜升起，在阳光下飘扬）

男孩：妹妹，让我们向国旗致敬。

          男孩和女孩在此唱道：-

          国旗在空中飘扬
          兄妹手牵手，
          向其三鞠躬。
          一鞠躬，愿国民革命成功，
          二鞠躬，愿帝国主义者失去其
                    傲慢，
          三鞠躬，扶弱抑强。

（一名朝鲜男孩和一名XX男孩从树后走近）

中国女孩：哥哥，来了两个矮子！
她的哥哥：让我们袭击这些矮子！

（左侧手写批注：）
特别处副督察

The XX Boy : Don't strike, don't strike me. Listen to what
I am going to sing :

My father is a tailor,
He works hard all day long.
But the cursed Fascist
Made my father join the war.
After fighting for less than a month,
My father died in battle.
My mother fled to China

Chinese Boy : The Fascists are our common enemy. We should
join hands and offer resistance! (Facing the
Korean boy). You Korean boy, what have you got

The Korean Boy sings :

I belong to a fisherman's family in Korea.
Our forefathers were from China.
The "devils" were unreasonable
And forced us to obey them.
They not only want us to fight China.
As it is unmanly to be ungrateful,
My father left home.
For this the unreasonable "devils" killed my mother.

Chinese Boy : So one of you has lost his father, while the other
has lost his mother. You two have suffered at
the hands of the Fascists. Here is our national
flag flying; it is your father and mother. Bow
before it and surrender yourselves to its embrace!

(The Korean and the XX boys make a bow)

Chinese Girl : Brother, since they all hate the XX militarists,
they are our brothers. Let us, hand in hand,
sing a song.

The others agree and the four dance and sing :

The Chinese national flag is flying in the air.
Although we four do not belong to the same people,
We are friends and good children.
Let us join hand in hand
And make three further bows to the Chinese flag.
First bow, may the national revolution succeed,
Second bow, may the Fascists lose their arrogance.
Third bow, help the weak and suppress the strong.
Let all children in the world join
And Overthrow the Nazi menace
Let all children in the world join
And overthrow the Nazi menace!

XX国男孩：别打，别打我。听我唱：

我的父亲是裁缝，
他终日辛勤劳作。

朝鲜男孩唱道：

我来自朝鲜的一个渔民家庭。
我们的祖先来自中国。
“鬼子”蛮横无理

推翻纳粹的威胁

May 10, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Standard of May 9s

THE DUTIES OF THE CHINESE CITIZENS TO-DAY
(Delivered by Chow Ung-lai 周恩来 and recorded by "Dick")
(Continued from May 8)

Our Duties

First of all we must realize that the present war of resistance will be a protracted struggle. We must not simply "drag" it along, but we must "fight" and "struggle" to the end. To do so we must accomplish the following:-
(1) Spiritually, we must be mobilized for a long war. In many places of China the spiritual mobilization movement has already achieved favourable results, but in some places signs of negligence are still to be noted. We should warn ourselves from time to time of the lukewarmness of our spirit and strengthen our anti-Japanese feeling.
(2) Militarily, we must concentrate on our work in the rear of the Japanese forces. At present, guerrilla fighting is the principal war tactics, because this will harass large numbers of Japanese soldiers and enable us to have at our command considerable military strength in the rear. At the final stage in the war of resistance, we shall recover our lost territory and drive out the Japanese soldiers.

Hopes on Youths

During the war of resistance, Chinese youths should not be afraid of hardships but should train themselves to be like "iron and steel" youths.
I have some points to offer to the youths throughout the country; our work will be carried out smoothly if we adopt
1) a determined stand in the war of resistance,
2) a frank, earnest and humble attitude,
3) a busy life to win the confidence of the community,
4) a determination to learn,
5) capacity of applying all our energy to a task.
In short, the principal duty confronting us is to develop the war of resistance to the stage when final victory is ensured.
If the war of resistance goes on as usual, there would be more hardships; however, we are not afraid of hardships, on the contrary, we shall welcome hardships for we shall overcome them!

(Reproduced from the "Singapore Daily News" of May 2)

1939年5月10日。下午译本。

《字林西报》五月九日版

今日中国公民之职责
（由周恩来讲述，“Dick”记录）
（续自五月八日）

我们的职责

首先，我们必须认识到，目前的抗战将是一场持久的斗争。我们不能仅仅“拖”下去，而必须“战斗”并“斗争”到底。为此，我们必须做到以下几点：
(1) 在精神上，我们必须为长期战争进行动员。在中国许多地方，精神动员运动已经取得了良好的成果，但在某些地方仍可看到疏忽的迹象。我们应该时常警惕自己精神上的懈怠，加强我们的抗日情绪。
(2) 在军事上，我们必须集中于日军后方的工作。目前，游击战是主要的作战战术，因为这将骚扰大量日军，并使我们在后方掌握可观的军事力量。在抗战的最后阶段，我们将收复失地，驱逐日军。

对青年的期望

在抗战期间，中国青年不应畏惧艰难困苦，而应将自己锻炼成如“钢铁”般的青年。
我对全国青年有几点建议；如果我们采取以下做法，我们的工作将会顺利开展：
1) 在抗战中立场坚定，
2) 态度坦率、诚恳且谦逊，
3) 过忙碌的生活以赢得社会的信任，
4) 决心学习，
5) 具备全力以赴完成任务的能力。
简而言之，摆在我们面前的主要职责是将抗战发展到确保最终胜利的阶段。
如果抗战照常进行，会有更多的艰难困苦；然而，我们并不害怕困难，相反，我们将欢迎困难，因为我们必将克服它们！

（转载自5月2日的《新加坡每日新闻》）

Date March 20, 1939.

Subject. News article containing allegation of three Japanese gendarmes
having been killed by hand grenades in Hongkew.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by _________________

（左侧手写批注：）
German
- Sei
Jho Robertson

In connection with the attached translation of
an article appearing in the Standard dated March 16
on the subject of three Japanese gendarmes having
been killed by hand grenades in front of the Dah Kong
Cotton Mill on Yangtszepoo Road on March 5, enquiries
have been made in the neighbourhood of the mill, 195
Tungyuen Road, including the staff of the Dong Tsung
(同春) Tea Shop opposite the mill, but no such
incident ever took place in that vicinity.

Regarding the attack on a foreman of the Lei
Foong Cotton Mill, enquiries have also been made.
The victim is a worker of the Lei Foong Silk Weaving
Factory, 83 Willow Road, named Woo Ka-fah (吳家法),
living at Lane 126, 9 Linching Road, and the incident
took place at the back door of his house at 8.45 p.m.
March 2. This case has no political significance,
being the outcome of personal differences between
the victim and his fellow workers. On March 3, the
detectives of the Yangtszepoo Station arrested two
suspects and are investigating the matter in the
usual way.

关于随附的3月16日《字林西报》上刊登的一篇文章的译文，该文主题是3月5日三名日本宪兵在杨树浦路大康纱厂门前被手榴弹炸死。已在该纱厂附近（包括对面同春茶店的员工）进行了查询，地址为通源路195号，但该附近从未发生过此类事件。

关于雷丰纱厂一名工头遇袭一事，也进行了查询。受害者是柳林路83号雷丰丝织厂的工人，名叫吴家法（Woo Ka-fah），住在临清路9弄126号，事件发生在3月2日晚8点45分其家后门。此案没有政治意义，是受害者与其同事之间个人矛盾的结果。3月3日，杨树浦警署的侦探逮捕了两名嫌疑人，并正在按常规方式调查此事。

Standard and other local newspapers:

3 JAPANESE GENDARMES KILLED BY HAND GRENADES IN
HONGKEW

On March 5 a disturbance took place in
Hongkew in which two Japanese were killed in front of the
Dah Kong Cotton Mill (大康纱厂) on Yangtszepoo Road.
Upon receipt of a report, the Japanese Special Naval
Landing Party immediately despatched a large number of
men to guard all the roads and to conduct a search,
while all traffic in the district north of the Soochow
Creek was held up.

According to information received from
Hongkew, it is said that during the trouble three Japanese
gendarmes were killed by hand grenades and that a foreman
of the Mei Foong Cotton Mill (美丰纱厂) was attacked with
an axe and seriously injured.

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

三名日本宪兵在虹口被手榴弹炸死

3月5日，虹口发生骚乱，两名日本人在杨树浦路大康纱厂门前被杀。
接到报告后，日本特别海军陆战队立即派遣大量人员守卫所有道路并进行搜查，同时苏州河以北地区的所有交通均被阻断。

据从虹口收到的消息，据说在骚乱期间，三名日本宪兵被手榴弹炸死，美丰纱厂的一名工头遭斧头袭击，身受重伤。
